editorial:
Imagine being a successful writer who gets trapped in a real-life crime story. You follow Charles Lattimore, a guy who wrote a book about a famous murder case, only to find himself as the main suspect when one of his students ends up dead. The vibe is very moody and tense, making you feel the pressure as he tries to prove he didn't do it. It feels like a classic mystery where you are constantly guessing who is lying and who is telling the truth, keeping you glued to your seat the whole time.

The acting is solid, and the way the mystery unfolds keeps the pace moving quickly without feeling rushed. One of the best parts is how it plays with your expectations regarding the book's original subject. While it is an older TV movie, the story holds up great. If you want to experience this, you should look for it on digital rental platforms like Apple TV or search for a physical copy to add to your collection. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you just want a good puzzle to solve.
endingExplained: You find out that Lattimore was indeed being framed by the person from his book. The killer tried to make it look like the professor committed the crime to get revenge for the book. In the final scenes, the evidence finally points away from Lattimore and toward the actual murderer. After a tense standoff, the truth comes out, the real killer is caught, and Lattimore is finally cleared of all charges.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school murder mysteries and whodunit stories.
